quiz.typeADesc: Your bloating pattern suggests that dairy products may be a key trigger. Many people struggle to digest lactose properly, which can cause bloating, gas, and discomfort after eating dairy.

quiz.typeCDesc: Your bloating pattern suggests that eating habits, meal timing, and stress may be key contributors. This type of bloating is often linked to how and when you eat, rather than specific foods.

about.heading: About me
about.journeyPara1: My journey into nutrition wasn't planned. It started at 16, when I was diagnosed with polycystic ovaries (PCOS). Alongside irregular cycles, I struggled with persistent acne — the kind that follows you into every photo and eats away at your confidence — and very few clear answers about why. Frustrated by symptoms I couldn't seem to fix, I went to university to study Pharmacology, hoping to understand the medicines I was being offered and, honestly, hoping science would give me a straightforward answer.
about.journeyPara2: Instead, over my degree I became more and more curious about what was happening beyond the pill bottle — how the body responds to food, sleep, stress, movement. I kept asking myself: what's the source? how can I actually prevent this? — questions medication alone couldn't answer for me.
journeyMilestones: Completed BSc Pharmacology at University of East Anglia
Studied Integrative and Preventive Nutrition at MIIN
Completed MSc in Dietetics at Teesside University
Registered as a Dietitian with the HCPC
Currently practising as a Gastroenterology Dietitian in the NHS
about.journeyClosing: Everything I went through as a teenager and in my twenties changed how I see health — not just what's on the plate, but the whole person around it. Personally, I noticed real improvements as I understood my own body better. In my clinical work, though, every recommendation I give is grounded in evidence and your individual picture. My more personal thoughts on the mind–body side of health sit in the section just below.
about.beyondBody1: Beyond my professional dietetic work, I have a strong personal interest in psychology and the mind–body connection. Writers like Lise Bourbeau — who explores the emotional roots of physical experience — resonate deeply with me. Books such as her Listen to Your Body have shaped how I think about wellbeing on a personal level.
about.beyondBody2: These are personal reflections, not clinical methods I use with my clients — my professional dietetic advice always stays firmly within evidence-based practice.
about.journeyPara3: That question led to years of reading, trying things, making mistakes, and slowly beginning to understand how much everyday habits shape how we feel. Somewhere in those years, I realised I wanted to help other people through the same confusion — not from a place of theory, but from someone who's genuinely been there.
about.journeyPara4: So I went back to university and completed my MSc in Dietetics at Teesside, becoming a Registered Dietitian. From there I spent 1.5 years working on hospital wards, supporting patients with a wide range of serious conditions — and it became clear where my heart was. Time and time again, I saw how much goes wrong when the gut–brain axis is out of balance, and I knew that gut health was where I wanted to focus.
about.journeyPara5: Today I work part-time as a Gastroenterology Dietitian within the NHS, supporting patients with IBS, coeliac disease, inflammatory bowel disease and other complex digestive conditions. I love my NHS work — but honestly, what draws me most is my private practice. It's where I get to build proper connections with the clients who choose to work with me, take the time to really listen, and shape care around their whole life.

consent.transparencyBody: Anna Doran Health (HCPC DT034558, ICO CSN1032456) is the data controller responsible for your information. I process it to provide you with safe dietetic care, under UK GDPR Article 6(1)(b) and Article 9(2)(h) — the lawful basis that applies to regulated health professionals. When you submit this form, your name, email and a record of the consents you gave are stored securely on my own server, along with the date and the version of this wording, because I am required to be able to demonstrate that consent was properly given. I am also sent a notification containing your name, email and which boxes you ticked — never any clinical information. Your records are retained for 8 years, in line with British Dietetic Association guidance. I use a small number of trusted third-party services to run the practice — full details are in my Privacy Policy. If you are ever unhappy with how your information is handled, please tell me first so I can put it right; you also have the right to raise the matter with the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk / 0303 123 1113).
consent.safeguardingBody: What you share with me is treated as confidential and used only to support your care. There are limited circumstances in which I may need to share information — for example, where there is a serious concern for your safety or someone else's, or where I am legally required to do so. If this ever arises, I will discuss it with you beforehand whenever possible.
consent.withdrawalBody: You can withdraw your consent at any time by emailing me at contact@annadorandiet.com. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing already carried out. If you withdraw the core consent, our dietetic relationship will end; the retention period stated above will still apply, as required by my professional body.
consent.title: Client Consent Form
consent.intro: Welcome. Before we begin working together, I'd like you to read through a few things — how I work, how I look after your information, and what to expect from your sessions. It should only take a couple of minutes.
consent.name: Full name
consent.consent1: I understand that consultations take place online via video call. Working remotely has limitations compared to meeting in person — Anna cannot physically examine me, and we rely on the information I provide about myself. Anna is a registered dietitian, not a medical doctor, and works within her professional scope of practice. If she identifies anything that requires urgent medical attention (for example significant unexplained weight loss, GI bleeding, severe pain, or signs of self-harm), she will ask me to contact my GP, NHS 111, or 999, and may pause our work together until I have been seen by a medical professional. Online consultations are not appropriate for medical emergencies.
consent.consent2: I confirm that I am 18 or over and have capacity to give my own consent. I agree that Anna Doran Health may collect and process my health information — including dietary details, symptoms, medical history, and food diaries — for the purpose of providing dietetic care. This is permitted under UK GDPR Article 6(1)(b) and Article 9(2)(h), the lawful basis that applies to regulated health professionals.
consent.consent3: I understand that results are not guaranteed and that everyone responds differently. Anna's advice is grounded in her professional expertise, but outcomes also depend on my individual circumstances and how I apply the recommendations in practice.
consent.consent4: I agree that Anna may contact my GP to share relevant information about our consultations and any dietary recommendations, where appropriate.
consent.note: By submitting this form, you are confirming that you have read and understood the above, and that you agree to my
consent.noteMiddle: . For full details on how your information is handled, please see my
consent.noteEnd: If you have any concerns about how your information has been handled, you have the right to raise them with the ICO (ico.org.uk) or the HCPC (hcpc-uk.org).
consent.successMessage: Thank you — your consent has been received. I will be in touch shortly to arrange your first session.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.intro: This cookie policy explains what cookies are, how this website uses them and similar storage technologies, and your choices.
cookies.whatAreCookies: Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website. Some websites, including this one, also use your browser's local storage, which works in a similar way. They help the site remember your preferences and improve your experience.
cookies.cookie1Purpose: Stores your language preference (English or Russian)
cookies.cookie2Purpose: Remembers that you have seen and answered the cookie notice (stored in your browser, not sent to my server)
cookies.cookie2Duration: Until you clear your browser storage
cookies.thirdParty: I use Google Analytics to see how many people visit the site and which pages are most useful. It is the only third-party service that sets cookies here, and it is switched off by default: the Google script is not loaded at all, and no Google cookie is created, unless and until you press 'Accept analytics'. If you choose 'Essential only', nothing is sent to Google. Google Analytics is configured to anonymise IP addresses, and I use it only to view general trends — I cannot identify individual visitors from it. Google processes some of this data in the United States under the UK extension to the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. There is no advertising pixel and no session-recording tool on this site.
cookies.howToDisable: As well as the 'Cookie settings' link on this site, you can block or delete cookies through your browser settings — check your browser's help section for instructions. Please note that disabling essential cookies may affect how the website functions. Google also offers a browser add-on that opts you out of Google Analytics on every site, at tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout.
cookies.contact: If you have any questions about this cookie policy, please contact me at contact@annadorandiet.com.
cookies.cookie3Purpose: Google Analytics — distinguishes one visitor from another so visits are not double-counted
cookies.cookie4Purpose: Google Analytics — keeps track of a single browsing session
cookies.changeMind: You can change your choice at any time using the 'Cookie settings' link at the bottom of every page. Choosing 'Essential only' after previously accepting will delete the Google Analytics cookies already on your device and stop any further data being collected.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.effectiveDate: Effective from 7 September 2026. This policy is regularly reviewed and updated.
privacy.intro: This privacy policy sets out how I, Anna Doran (Anna Doran Health), use and protect any personal information that you provide to me. Should I ask you to provide certain information by which you can be identified when using my services, you can be assured that it will only be used in accordance with this privacy policy and the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR).
privacy.whyCollect: I collect your personal data so that I can provide my independent nutrition and dietetic services to you, and so that I can reply when you get in touch. Separately, if you have ticked the box to ask for it, I use your email address to send you my newsletter. The legal grounds for each of these are set out in the next section.
privacy.lawfulBasis: I process your personal data under Article 6(1)(b) UK GDPR (performance of a contract) when you book a paid service, and Article 6(1)(a) (consent) for the newsletter and contact form enquiries.
privacy.lawfulBasisHealth: Health and dietary information is special category data under Article 9 UK GDPR. As an HCPC-registered dietitian, I process this data under Article 9(2)(h) (provision of health care by a health professional under a duty of confidentiality), read with Schedule 1 Part 1 paragraph 2 of the Data Protection Act 2018. Where I share information with your GP or another healthcare professional, I will obtain your separate explicit consent (Article 9(2)(a)) before doing so.
privacy.collect1: Name, date of birth, age, sex, next of kin, GP name and address, marital status, living arrangements and occupation.

privacy.usedFor2: Sharing information with relevant healthcare professionals such as your GP or medical team (your separate consent will always be obtained before this is done).
privacy.usedForException: In exceptional circumstances, information about a client may be disclosed without consent if it is in the public interest to do so. This might be in circumstances where disclosing the information is necessary to prevent a serious crime or serious harm to other people.
privacy.websiteDataHeading: What information is collected via this website
privacy.websiteData1: This website uses Google Analytics to help me understand how the site is used — for example which pages are most read. It is entirely optional: no analytics cookie is set and no data is sent to Google unless you press 'Accept analytics' on the cookie notice, and you can change your mind at any time using the 'Cookie settings' link in the footer. IP addresses are anonymised, and I only ever see general trends, never individual visitors. There is no advertising pixel or session-recording tool on this site. My hosting provider also keeps standard server logs for security and reliability purposes.
privacy.websiteData2: This website uses cookies to help provide a better user experience. Please see my <link>Cookie Policy</link> for full details. You may disable cookies in your browser if you prefer.
privacy.websiteData3: You can subscribe to my newsletter from the signup form, the bloating quiz or the enquiry form. In every case it is a separate, optional tick box — I will never add you to the list because you contacted me or took the quiz. Your name and email are stored in MailerLite and used only to send you updates, and you can unsubscribe from any email at any time.
privacy.websiteData4: When you submit the contact form, your name, email, phone number, selected service and message are saved securely on my own server. A short notification is sent to me via Telegram so that I can respond promptly. That notification contains only your first name, the service you selected and how you would prefer to be contacted. Telegram is operated outside the UK; see 'Sending data outside the UK' below.
privacy.thirdPartyIntro: I use the following third-party services to operate my business. Each provider has their own privacy policy and data protection measures:

privacy.thirdParty2: MailerLite — email newsletter. Your name and email are stored to send you nutrition updates you have subscribed to.

privacy.thirdParty6: Google Workspace — my professional email (contact@annadorandiet.com), client contact records (Google Sheets) and client documents (Google Drive) are hosted on Google Workspace under Google's Data Processing Addendum. My subscription does not include regional data storage, so some of this processing may take place outside the UK; see 'Sending data outside the UK' below.
privacy.control1: I will not distribute, sell or lease your personal information to third parties unless I have your explicit permission or am required by law to do so.
privacy.control2: You may request details of personal information which I hold about you under the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR). If you believe that any information I am holding on you is incorrect or incomplete, please contact me as soon as possible and I will promptly correct it.
privacy.control3: All service providers used to store and process information related to carrying out dietetic services have robust security procedures in place and are GDPR compliant. BDA and HCPC record-keeping guidelines are strictly adhered to for one-to-one consultations.
privacy.retention: Records relating to the care of a client will be stored for eight years, in line with British Dietetic Association Guidance for Records and Record Keeping. Contact form enquiries and bloating quiz records are retained for 12 months. Payment records are retained for six years in accordance with HMRC requirements.

privacy.right3: The right to request deletion of your data (right to be forgotten).
privacy.right4: The right to restrict or object to processing of your data.
privacy.right6: The right to withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal.
privacy.rightsICO: If you are unhappy with how your data has been handled, you have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk.
privacy.controller: I (Anna Doran, HCPC registered dietitian) am the data controller at Anna Doran Health. Please contact me at contact@annadorandiet.com with any queries or requests related to your personal data and I will respond promptly.
privacy.thirdParty7: Cal.com — booking scheduler for free discovery calls. Cal.com stores your name, email and appointment time under its own GDPR-aligned Data Processing Agreement.
privacy.thirdParty8: WhatsApp Business — used for direct client communication (appointment logistics only, no clinical or health data). Messages are end-to-end encrypted. WhatsApp is operated by Meta Platforms Ireland under its own Data Processing Agreement.

The quiz is a general educational tool, not a diagnosis or an assessment of your health. You can ask me to delete your quiz record at any time.

I keep this because data protection law requires me to be able to show that consent was properly given.
privacy.transfers: Most of your information stays in the UK or the European Economic Area. My website and its database are held on servers in Europe. Some of the services I use process data further afield, and I set each of them out honestly below.
privacy.securityHeading: How I keep your information safe
privacy.security: I take the security of your information seriously. All data sent to and from this website is encrypted in transit. Client records are held in access-controlled accounts protected by strong, unique passwords and two-factor authentication, on devices that are encrypted and kept up to date. Access is limited to me alone. Payment card details never reach my systems at all. If a data breach were ever to occur that posed a risk to your rights, I would report it to the ICO within 72 hours and tell you directly where required.
privacy.automated: I do not make any decisions about you by automated means, and I do not carry out profiling that produces legal or similarly significant effects. Website analytics are viewed only as aggregate trends and are never used to make decisions about an individual. The bloating quiz sorts your answers into a general category for educational purposes only — every clinical judgement about your care is made by me personally.
privacy.complaints: If you have any concern about how your information has been handled, please contact me first at contact@annadorandiet.com so that I can put it right. I aim to respond within five working days and to resolve matters within one month. If you are not satisfied with my response, you have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113. You may also raise concerns about my professional practice with the Health and Care Professions Council at hcpc-uk.org.
privacy.changes: I review this policy regularly and will update it whenever my services or the tools I use change. The effective date at the top of this page always shows when it was last revised. Where a change materially affects how your information is used, I will tell existing clients directly.
privacy.businessInfo5: Postal address for data protection queries: available on request by emailing contact@annadorandiet.com
privacy.thirdParty9: Google Analytics — optional website statistics, active only if you accept analytics cookies. It records anonymised information such as pages viewed, approximate region and device type. Google LLC processes some of this data in the United States under the UK extension to the EU–US Data Privacy Framework.
privacy.transfers2: Google — Google LLC processes anonymised website statistics in the United States. My Google Workspace subscription, which holds my email, client records and documents, does not include regional data storage, so some of that processing may also take place outside the UK. Google is certified under the UK Extension to the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, which the UK government recognises as providing adequate protection, and applies the UK International Data Transfer Addendum to other transfers. WhatsApp Business is provided by Meta Platforms Ireland, based in the European Economic Area; messages are end-to-end encrypted, and Meta relies on the Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses for any onward processing in the United States.
privacy.transfers3: Telegram — used only to alert me that a form has been submitted. Telegram FZ-LLC is based in the United Arab Emirates, which is not covered by a UK adequacy decision, and Telegram does not offer a data processing agreement or International Data Transfer Agreement for its notification service. For that reason I keep these notifications to the minimum that is useful: a first name, the service you chose and how you would like me to reply. Your surname, email address, phone number and message never leave my own server, and I read every enquiry in my admin system rather than in Telegram.
privacy.transfers4: You are never obliged to use Telegram or WhatsApp, and you do not have to use the contact form at all. If you would prefer that none of your information leaves the UK, email me directly at contact@annadorandiet.com and I will handle your enquiry that way.
privacy.insuranceHeading: If you use private medical insurance
privacy.insurance: If you claim through a private medical insurer, I share information with them so that your care can be invoiced. This normally includes your name, date of birth, policy and authorisation numbers, the dates and type of your appointments, and the clinical codes describing your treatment. I share it only with your own insurer, and only with your separate explicit consent under Article 9(2)(a) UK GDPR, which you give on my client consent form.
privacy.insurance2: Your insurer decides for itself how it uses your information, so it acts as an independent data controller and its own privacy policy applies alongside mine. Your insurer may also send me information about you, such as your policy details and authorisation for treatment. You are never obliged to claim on insurance — you are always welcome to pay for your appointments directly.
privacy.thirdParty10: Healthcode — the secure system used across UK private healthcare to submit invoices to insurers. If you claim on insurance, your billing and appointment details pass through Healthcode. It is a UK company and this data stays in the UK.
